world: Two unrelated fictional job candidates and the roles they are interviewing for. Candidate A, Advik Thorambath, is a backend and distributed-systems engineer in Hyderabad with six years of experience (Quillhaven Freight Systems since March 2023, Tessarine Mobility before that) who works in Go and Kotlin on PostgreSQL and Kafka; he is interviewing for Senior Backend Engineer, Payments & Ledger, on the Ledger Core team of Ostrakel Payments in Bengaluru. Candidate B, Catarina Velmonte, is a lead frontend and product engineer in Porto with nine years of experience (Lumenquay since June 2022, Ondaverde Health and Plumewright Studio before that) who works in React, TypeScript and Vue with a focus on accessibility, design systems, frontend performance and product experimentation; she is interviewing for Senior Product Engineer, Collaborative AI Workspace, on the Workspace Surface squad of Hollowpine Labs (Rotterdam, remote within Europe). The two candidates share no employer, project, city, university, technology emphasis or metric value. Neither résumé nor job description states the candidate's reason for leaving, relocation preference, notice period, salary expectation, visa status, weaknesses, or any conflict, failure or mentoring story.

files.title: Résumé of Advik Thorambath, Senior Software Engineer (backend and distributed systems)

facts.statement: The candidate's name is Advik Thorambath.
Advik lives in Hyderabad, Telangana, India.
Advik has six years of experience as a backend engineer (first job started July 2020).
Advik's core stack is Go and Kotlin on PostgreSQL and Kafka.
Advik's current employer is Quillhaven Freight Systems in Hyderabad.
Quillhaven Freight Systems is a freight dispatch and shipment-tracking platform used by about 1,900 regional trucking carriers.
Advik has been Senior Software Engineer and Tech Lead of the Dispatch Core team at Quillhaven since April 2024.
As tech lead of Dispatch Core, a team of five, Advik leads 4 engineers, owns the technical roadmap, runs the weekly design review and signs off the production-readiness checklist.
Advik joined Quillhaven as Software Engineer II and held that title from March 2023 to March 2024.
Advik's previous employer was Tessarine Mobility in Pune, where he was a Software Engineer from July 2020 to February 2023.
Tessarine Mobility is an intercity bus ticketing platform selling about 55,000 tickets a day.
Skeinrouter is the Go and Kafka event pipeline Advik designed and led at Quillhaven; it replaced the cron-polled tracking module of the monolith, which polled carrier integrations every 60 seconds.
Skeinrouter ran from June 2024 to February 2025, with Advik as tech lead of 4 engineers and author of the design document.
Skeinrouter raised peak throughput from 9,000 to 41,000 events per second.
Skeinrouter cut p99 end-to-end latency from 870 ms to 140 ms.

Skeinrouter is built as Go 1.22 services consuming from Kafka with 48 partitions on the main topic keyed by shipment ID, an outbox table in PostgreSQL for webhooks, and backpressure by pausing partitions.
Advik personally built Skeinrouter's partitioning and ordering scheme, the shared consumer framework and the deduplication layer, and reviewed every change to the delivery path.
Skeinrouter was rolled out with 6 weeks of shadow traffic and then per-carrier flags over 9 weeks, with no rollback.
Advik made every Skeinrouter consumer idempotent with a PostgreSQL deduplication table keyed on event ID and carrier ID, cutting duplicate status webhooks from 0.6% of deliveries to under 0.01%.
Advik is primary on-call for the dispatch domain one week in five and has been incident commander for 9 Sev-1 and Sev-2 incidents since April 2024.

Advik led the response to the November 2024 consumer-lag incident, a rebalance storm that delayed tracking updates for 3 hours 40 minutes, and the follow-up that moved all consumer groups to cooperative rebalancing with static membership.
The reliability programme Advik ran took Sev-1 incidents in the dispatch domain from 14 in 2023 to 5 in 2025.
The reliability programme cut median time to restore from 52 minutes to 19 minutes; Advik wrote 17 runbooks and replaced threshold alerts with SLO burn-rate alerts.
Advik cut p95 latency of Quillhaven's load-search API from 310 ms to 85 ms with keyset pagination and two covering indexes.
Marrowgate was the migration of Quillhaven's dispatch datastore from sharded MySQL 5.7 to PostgreSQL 15; Advik owned its design document and cutover runbook.
Marrowgate ran from August 2023 to February 2024; Advik was design owner, working with 2 other engineers and 1 database administrator.
Marrowgate moved 2.3 TB in 410 tables across 6 MySQL shards into one PostgreSQL 15 cluster on Amazon RDS with monthly table partitioning.

Marrowgate used change data capture with Debezium through Kafka for the backfill, dual writes for 5 weeks, and nightly row-level checksum comparison until mismatches stayed at zero for 10 consecutive nights.
The Marrowgate cutover took one 11-minute read-only window on a Sunday morning, with no data-loss incident and no rollback.
Marrowgate lowered database spend from USD 18,400 to USD 12,700 per month, 31% lower, and removed the shard-routing library from 8 services.
Farecrest is the fare-quote service Advik built and operated at Tessarine Mobility in Kotlin on Ktor with PostgreSQL and a Redis cache, in 2021 and 2022.

On Farecrest Advik was one of 3 engineers and owned caching and query performance: removed N+1 queries, added partial indexes, put PgBouncer in transaction mode, and introduced a two-tier cache with event-driven invalidation.
Farecrest p95 latency went from 480 ms to 95 ms at a festival-season peak of 3,200 requests per second.
After the latency work the Farecrest fleet was reduced from 36 to 22 instances.
At Tessarine Advik replaced application-level seat holds with PostgreSQL advisory locks, taking double bookings from 37 a month to fewer than 2.
At Tessarine Advik moved booking events from RabbitMQ to Kafka (12 topics) with a two-week dual-publish period; it was the company's first production Kafka cluster.
At Tessarine Advik joined the backend on-call rotation in his second year and carried the booking-path pager through two festival seasons.
At Quillhaven Advik built the carrier rate-limiting middleware in Go (token bucket backed by Redis) that sits in front of all 23 public API endpoints.
Advik added OpenTelemetry tracing across the 8 dispatch services and built the Grafana dashboards used by the on-call engineer.
pgslotwatch is Advik's open-source Go command-line tool (2022) that reports PostgreSQL replication-slot lag; it has about 260 GitHub stars.
Advik's listed languages are Go, Kotlin and SQL, with Python for scripts and tooling.
Advik's listed data and messaging skills are PostgreSQL, Kafka, Redis, Debezium and MySQL.
Advik's listed infrastructure and observability skills are Kubernetes, AWS (EKS, RDS, MSK), Terraform, Prometheus, Grafana and OpenTelemetry.
Advik holds a Bachelor of Technology in Computer Science and Engineering from Kesavadri Institute of Technology, Warangal (2016 to 2020), CGPA 8.41 out of 10.
Advik's final-year project was a Raft-based key-value store written in Go.
Advik holds the AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Associate certification (2022).
Advik spoke at the Hyderabad Go meetup in March 2025 on ordering guarantees in Kafka.
Advik speaks English, Telugu and Hindi.

must_not_infer: The résumé does not state any Java experience; Kotlin on Ktor is the only JVM work listed.
The résumé does not state any payments, ledger, banking, accounting or reconciliation experience; the domains are freight dispatch and bus ticketing.
The résumé does not mention PCI DSS or any other compliance standard.
The résumé does not say whether Advik is willing to relocate (to Bengaluru or anywhere) or to work hybrid.
The résumé does not state why Advik is leaving or wants to leave Quillhaven, nor why he left Tessarine Mobility.
The résumé does not state a notice period, an availability date, a current salary or a salary expectation.
The résumé does not state weaknesses, and contains no conflict, failure or mentoring story; leading 4 engineers is stated as scope, not as people management or mentoring.
The résumé does not say Advik has line-management responsibility, hiring responsibility or budget ownership.
The November 2024 incident is described only by cause, duration and follow-up; the résumé does not say who caused it or that Advik caused it.
Idempotent consumers and an outbox table are stated; idempotency keys on public money-moving APIs are not.

files.title: Ostrakel Payments job description: Senior Backend Engineer, Payments & Ledger (Ledger Core team, Bengaluru)

facts.statement: The hiring company is Ostrakel Payments, which builds payment orchestration and merchant-ledger infrastructure for mid-market marketplaces in India and Southeast Asia.
The role title is Senior Backend Engineer, Payments & Ledger.
The role is on the Ledger Core team, which owns the double-entry ledger, the idempotency layer in front of every money-moving API, and the daily reconciliation.
Ledger Core has 9 engineers: 7 backend engineers and 2 site reliability engineers.
The role reports to Sarvesh Idnavalli, Engineering Manager for Ledger Core.
The role is based at Ostrakel's Bengaluru office in HSR Layout.
Work is hybrid: three days a week in the office, Tuesday to Thursday.
The role is not open to fully remote candidates.
Relocation assistance is available for candidates moving to Bengaluru from another city.
The role is a senior individual-contributor role at level L5; the next level, L6, is Staff Engineer.
Ostrakel was founded in 2019, has about 420 people, and serves more than 3,100 marketplaces.
Ostrakel processes 2.6 million transactions on an ordinary day and settles through 13 partner banks.
New Ledger Core services are written in Go 1.23.
The settlement engine and reconciliation batch jobs are Java 21 on Spring Boot and make up roughly 40% of the team's code, so the engineer works in both Go and Java.
The role must keep money movement exactly-once in effect: idempotency keys on every write API, an outbox per service, and safely replayable consumers.
doc_needles: idempotency keys on every write API

facts.statement: The ledger runs on PostgreSQL 16 with partitioned journal tables and serializable transactions where needed.
A Kafka backbone carries ledger events to settlement, risk and reporting.
The three-way reconciliation pipeline has an unexplained break rate of 0.05% of transactions today, with a goal of below 0.02% this financial year.
On-call is one week in six as primary for Ledger Core, around the clock, with a compensatory day off after each on-call week.
The engineer leads design reviews and guides 2 to 3 engineers; the role has no line-management duties.
Must have: 6 or more years of backend engineering, with at least 2 of them at senior level or as technical lead of a team.
Must have: production experience in Go or Java, and willingness to work in both.
doc_needles: Production experience in Go or Java

facts.statement: Must have: at least 2 years building payment, ledger, banking or other money-movement systems.
Must have: deep PostgreSQL knowledge of transaction isolation, locking, indexing and partitioning.
Must have: hands-on work with Kafka or a comparable log, including ordering, consumer groups and delivery semantics.
Must have: a record of designing for idempotency, retries and partial failure in distributed systems.
Must have: experience carrying the pager for a tier-1 service and leading incident response.
Must have: ownership, having taken a system from design document to production and stayed with it afterwards.
Good to have: Java and Spring Boot in production.
doc_needles: Java and Spring Boot in production

facts.statement: Good to have: working knowledge of PCI DSS v4.0; Ostrakel is a certified PCI DSS Level 1 service provider and Ledger Core services are in audit scope.
Good to have: having built or run a reconciliation system, or a working understanding of double-entry accounting.
doc_needles: built or run a reconciliation system

facts.statement: Good to have: familiarity with UPI and card settlement flows, or with ISO 20022 messages.
Good to have: zero-downtime data migrations and change data capture.
The interview process is a 30-minute recruiter call followed by four rounds, usually completed within three weeks.

The interview rounds are: coding (60 minutes, in Go or Java), system design (75 minutes, on a ledger or payment flow), a deep dive into a system the candidate built and ran, and a hiring-manager conversation.
Benefits include health insurance for dependants, an annual learning budget of INR 60,000, employee stock options and 26 days of paid leave a year.
Compensation is fixed pay plus stock options; the L5 band is not published in the posting and is shared during the recruiter call.
The posting is requisition OST-ENG-0417, posted 14 September 2026.

must_not_infer: The job description states no salary figure or band; it must not be read as a salary offer or as the candidate's expectation.
Relocation assistance being available says nothing about whether the candidate is willing to relocate, and no amount is stated.
The job description says nothing about the candidate: it does not say Advik meets or fails any requirement.
The job description does not state a notice-period limit, a start date or a visa or work-authorisation requirement.
Java is required as 'Go or Java, and willingness to work in both'; Java and Spring Boot in production is only a good-to-have, so lack of Java is a gap to learn, not a stated disqualifier.
The 2-year payments or money-movement requirement is a must-have; the posting does not say whether adjacent experience can substitute for it.
PCI DSS knowledge is a good-to-have, not a must-have.

files.title: CV of Catarina Velmonte, Lead Frontend Engineer (product engineering)

facts.statement: The candidate's name is Catarina Velmonte.
Catarina lives in Porto, Portugal.
Catarina has nine years of experience as a frontend engineer (first job started September 2017).
Catarina's last four years have been in React and TypeScript and the earlier five mostly in Vue.
Catarina's core stack is React, TypeScript and Vue, with accessibility, design systems, frontend performance and product experimentation as her focus.
Catarina's current employer is Lumenquay, a remote-first company in Porto.
Lumenquay makes scheduling and client-messaging software for veterinary clinics, used by about 2,700 clinics.
Catarina has been Lead Frontend Engineer at Lumenquay since January 2024.

Catarina leads the frontend chapter of 18 engineers across 5 product squads and works day to day in the booking squad of 6; she sets frontend standards, runs the fortnightly architecture forum and owns the frontend hiring loop.
Catarina joined Lumenquay as Senior Frontend Engineer and held that title from June 2022 to December 2023.
Before Lumenquay Catarina was a Frontend Engineer at Ondaverde Health in Lisbon from February 2020 to May 2022.
Catarina's first job was Junior Web Developer at Plumewright Studio, a digital agency in Braga, from September 2017 to January 2020.
Pebblekit is the Lumenquay design system Catarina founded and leads: 64 components in React and TypeScript, documented in Storybook, with design tokens generated from Figma variables.
Catarina leads the Pebblekit working group of 3 engineers and 2 designers (2023 to present).
Pebblekit is adopted by all 5 product squads and used in 3 applications: the clinic web app, the pet-owner booking flow and the internal admin.
Every Pebblekit component meets WCAG 2.2 AA; axe-core checks and keyboard-interaction specs run in CI on every pull request.
Automated accessibility violations across the Lumenquay product fell from 212 to 9 in the year after Pebblekit adoption.
Fernlatch was the rebuild of Lumenquay's pet-owner booking flow, from September 2022 to April 2023, with Catarina as tech lead of 3 frontend engineers working with 1 designer.
Fernlatch was rebuilt in React and TypeScript with server rendering on Next.js, route-level code splitting and build-time image sizing.
Fernlatch took mobile p75 LCP from 4.3 s to 1.7 s.
Fernlatch took interaction delay from 380 ms to 120 ms.
Fernlatch took JavaScript on first load from 1.9 MB to 610 kB.
Booking completion rose from 61.2% to 66.8% with Fernlatch, measured in a six-week A/B experiment against the old flow.

Dialbench is the in-house experimentation toolkit Catarina wrote at Lumenquay in 2024: a feature-flag and A/B assignment service in Node.js on Fastify plus a React hooks SDK, with exposure events sent to Amplitude.
Catarina was sole author of the first version of Dialbench; it is now maintained with 1 backend engineer.
doc_needles: sole author of the first version

facts.statement: 38 experiments ran on Dialbench in its first year, each with a written hypothesis, a primary metric and guardrail metrics agreed before launch.
One Dialbench experiment, the reminder opt-in redesign, raised opt-in from 27% to 33%.
Catarina defined Lumenquay's product analytics taxonomy of 96 tracked events with typed payloads, so a renamed event fails the build.
Catarina moved the Lumenquay clinic web app from JavaScript to TypeScript strict mode: 1,150 files over 5 months with no release freeze.
Catarina introduced Lighthouse CI performance budgets that block a pull request adding more than 25 kB to the booking route.
At Ondaverde Health Catarina led the move of Farolim, the patient portal, from Vue 2 to Vue 3: 140 views, Vuex replaced by Pinia, done in 8 months alongside normal feature work.
The Farolim migration replaced Vuex with Pinia and took 8 months.
Unit coverage of the Farolim portal rose from 34% to 71% during the rewrite.
Catarina ran the accessibility remediation of the Farolim portal; it passed an external WCAG 2.1 AA audit in March 2022, with manual checks in NVDA and VoiceOver.
At Plumewright Studio Catarina built more than 20 marketing sites and 4 online storefronts in Vue 2 and plain JavaScript.
Catarina runs a weekly accessibility triage with design and support and reviews every new pattern for keyboard and screen-reader behaviour.
Catarina's listed frontend skills are React, TypeScript, Vue 3, Next.js and modern CSS.
Catarina's listed quality tooling is Playwright, Vitest, axe-core, Storybook and Lighthouse CI.
Catarina's backend skills are listed as light: Node.js, Fastify and GraphQL clients.
Catarina holds a Licenciatura (BSc) in Informatics Engineering from Instituto Superior de Valdouro, Braga (2014 to 2017), final grade 16 out of 20.
Catarina holds the IAAP Web Accessibility Specialist (WAS) certification, 2023.
Catarina gave the talk Design tokens that survive a rebrand at the Porto Frontend Meetup in October 2024.
Catarina speaks Portuguese (native), English (fluent) and Spanish (intermediate).

must_not_infer: The CV does not state any real-time collaboration, multiplayer, WebSocket, CRDT or operational-transform experience.
The CV does not state any AI, LLM, streaming-response or prompt work.
The CV does not state experience with rich-text editor frameworks, Canvas or WebGL.
Node.js is listed as light backend work (one small assignment service); the CV does not claim backend or infrastructure seniority.
The CV does not say whether Catarina is willing to relocate or travel, and does not state her nationality, citizenship, visa status or right to work.
The CV does not state why Catarina wants to leave Lumenquay or why she left Ondaverde Health or Plumewright Studio.
The CV does not state a notice period, an availability date, a current salary or a salary expectation.
The CV does not state weaknesses, and contains no conflict, failure or mentoring story; leading a chapter of 18 engineers is stated as scope, and the CV does not say she is their line manager.
The CV does not say the React work began before June 2022; the Ondaverde and Plumewright work is stated as Vue.

files.title: Hollowpine Labs job posting: Senior Product Engineer, Collaborative AI Workspace (Workspace Surface squad)

facts.statement: The hiring company is Hollowpine Labs.
The role title is Senior Product Engineer, Collaborative AI Workspace.
Hollowpine's product is Inkwharf, a collaborative workspace for writing, planning and sketching with an AI assistant built into the document.
Hollowpine Labs has 85 people, is Series B funded, and Inkwharf is used by about 8,500 teams.
The role is in Workspace Surface, the squad that owns the editor, the multiplayer layer and the assistant's in-document interface: 7 engineers, 2 designers and 1 product manager.
The role reports to Jorrit Aldewyck, Head of Product Engineering.
The company is based in Rotterdam, Netherlands; the role is remote within Europe.
Remote work must be in time zones UTC-1 to UTC+3, with core hours from 10:00 to 15:00 CET.
The Rotterdam hub is optional; nobody is required to use it.
doc_needles: nobody is required to use it

facts.statement: The whole team meets in Rotterdam for 4 team weeks a year, with travel and hotel paid.
There is no pager rotation; each engineer is support captain for one week every 7 weeks, during working hours only.
Candidates need the right to work in the European Union; Hollowpine cannot sponsor visas for this role.
Real-time UI work: presence, live cursors, comments and conflict-free editing on a CRDT layer (Yjs over WebSockets), in documents with up to 50 people editing at once.

AI UX work: streamed assistant responses in the document, inline suggestions the user can accept, reject or undo, citations back to the source blocks, and honest states for slow, partial or failed generations.
doc_needles: citations back to the source blocks

facts.statement: Accessibility work: the whole workspace to WCAG 2.2 AA, including making a multiplayer editor usable with a screen reader.
Experimentation: the team ships behind flags and runs around 10 experiments a quarter; the activation metric is a first shared document within 7 days of sign-up.
Performance targets: interaction delay under 200 ms at p75 on a 500-block document, and an initial JavaScript payload under 350 kB.
Required: 6+ years of professional frontend or product engineering, including at least 4 years of React and TypeScript in production.
Required: having shipped real-time collaborative or multiplayer features (WebSockets, CRDTs or operational transforms).
Required: accessibility work beyond linting, having taken a complex interface through an audit and fixed what it found.
Required: having designed, run and read product experiments, and knowing when a result should not be trusted.
doc_needles: designed, run and read product experiments

facts.statement: Required: a record of measured frontend performance improvements on real devices.
Required: product judgement, turning a vague customer problem into a small first version.
Nice to have: having shipped LLM-powered features (streaming interfaces, prompt iteration, or evaluation work with a model team).
Nice to have: experience with a rich-text editor framework (ProseMirror, Tiptap or Lexical).
Nice to have: having built or maintained a design system.
doc_needles: built or maintained a design system

facts.statement: Nice to have: some Node.js; the backend-for-frontend is a Node.js service that product engineers change regularly.
Nice to have: Canvas or WebGL rendering.

The hiring process has four steps: a 25-minute intro call, a 90-minute pairing session on a small React exercise, a 45-minute product and design critique, and conversations with two future teammates; most candidates finish in two weeks.
Benefits: 28 days of holiday a year, a home-office budget of EUR 1,500 in the first year, a learning budget of EUR 2,000 a year, and share options.
The salary band is not published in the posting; it is shared in the intro call.
The posting is reference HPL-2026-031, posted 22 September 2026.

must_not_infer: The posting states no salary figure or band; it must not be read as a salary offer or as the candidate's expectation.
The posting requires the right to work in the EU and offers no visa sponsorship, but says nothing about the candidate's own nationality, visa status or right to work.
The posting does not require relocation to Rotterdam; it says nothing about whether the candidate is willing to travel for the 4 team weeks.
The posting says nothing about the candidate: it does not say Catarina meets or fails any requirement.
Real-time collaborative experience is a requirement; the posting does not say whether other experience can substitute for it.
LLM-powered feature experience, rich-text editor frameworks, Canvas or WebGL are nice-to-haves, not requirements.
The posting does not state a notice-period limit or a start date.
